summary: Unifies spec traversal, but has crash risks and silent symlink skips.

findings.title: Silent exclusion of directory symlinks
findings.issue: The is_real_dir helper uses std::fs::symlink_metadata to block directory symlinks and prevent cycles. While cycle-avoidance is required, this implementation unconditionally skips all directory symlinks, including non-cyclic ones pointing to shared capability paths elsewhere. These directories and their specs are silently skipped during validation and archiving without raising warnings or errors.
findings.fix: Track visited directories (using device/inode numbers on Unix or canonical paths) to detect cycles during the recursive descent, or log a warning to stderr when skipping a symlinked directory.

findings.title: Crash when directory named spec.md exists
findings.issue: Inside collect_delta_specs_into, the collector unconditionally attempts to read dir.join("spec.md") as a file before verifying its file type. If a directory named spec.md exists (e.g. if the user names a capability spec.md), std::fs::read_to_string fails with a hard EISDIR error (which is not mapped to ErrorKind::NotFound), propagating the error and crashing the whole CLI execution.
findings.fix: Verify that dir.join("spec.md") exists and is a file (using metadata/symlink_metadata) before calling read_optional.

findings.title: Missing test for UTF-8 capability validation
findings.issue: The capability_id helper enforces strict UTF-8 paths, raising a hard error rather than fallback lossy conversion to ensure archive does not write to corrupted target paths. Although this is a critical design change, there are no tests verifying that invalid UTF-8 capability directory names successfully trigger this error path.
findings.fix: Add a test (e.g., under Unix-specific cfg) that creates a non-UTF-8 directory name under specs/ and asserts that validation/archiving fails with the expected error.

findings.title: Redundant sorting of applied results
findings.issue: In apply_spec_deltas, the final results are sorted via results.sort_by(|a, b| a.capability.cmp(&b.capability)). However, the shared collector collect_delta_specs already yields entries sorted by capability ID, rendering the second sort redundant.
findings.fix: Remove the redundant results.sort_by sorting line.
